controls.rule: Submitting evidence, suggesting changes, commenting, flagging and suggesting sources all require a signed-in user.
A user acting on behalf of an organization (contributing or moderating) must be a member of that organization; a user in several organizations must name one.
Accounts created via OAuth with a specific e-mail address or an @genome.wustl.edu address are automatically given the admin role (full moderation rights).
An optional comment supplied with an evidence submission must be at least 10 characters.
A submission is refused if a submitted or accepted evidence item with identical fields already exists.
A submission is refused when its source is marked retracted or deprecated, or its molecular profile, disease or therapies are deprecated.

controls.rule: An admin may accept their own suggested change.
The suggester may reject (withdraw) their own suggested change/revision without the editor role or COI.
The submitter of a still-submitted evidence item or assertion may accept revisions to it without the editor role or COI.
The suggester (or a moderator/editor) may edit a pending suggested change.
A change/revision that is no longer pending (already applied, or in S3-S4 any non-new status) cannot be accepted or rejected again.
Applying a suggested change is refused if the object's current values no longer match the values recorded when the change was suggested, unless the moderator passes force.

controls.rule: Raising a flag requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
Raising a flag sets the flagged marker on the flagged entity.
A flag may be resolved only by the user who raised it or by an editor with a valid COI statement.
Resolving a flag requires a comment of at least 10 characters.
Only an open flag can be resolved.
When the last open flag on an entity is resolved, the entity's flagged marker is cleared.
Background and scheduled jobs raise flags as the CIViCBot user on entities with data problems (duplicate allele registry IDs, obsolete ontology terms, Entrez symbol clean-up, fusion coordinates).

controls.rule: An assertion must be internally consistent for its type (significance, direction, disease, drugs/therapies, ACMG/AMP codes, NCCN version format).
Evidence items linked to an assertion must currently pass validation, and at least one evidence item is required except for Oncogenic assertions.
Only editors may accept an assertion.
Accepting or rejecting another user's assertion requires a valid COI statement.
Assertion moderation buttons are shown only to editors with a valid COI statement, but the server does not check COI.
A user may not accept an assertion they submitted.

controls.rule: The submitter may reject (withdraw) their own assertion without the editor role.
Rejecting or reverting an assertion requires a comment and accepting must not carry one.
A status change is refused if the assertion already has the requested status.
A rejected assertion is reset to submitted when a change is suggested or a suggested change is accepted.
Soft-deleting an assertion requires an editor with a valid COI statement.
An organizational approval of an assertion may be given only by a member of an organization with approval privileges who holds a valid COI statement.
An assertion can be approved only if it is accepted, not flagged, and has no active approval from the same organization.

Active organizational approvals are automatically set to requires_review when a revision to the assertion or a linked evidence item is accepted, a linked evidence item or the assertion is rejected, or the assertion is flagged.
Revoking an approval requires approval privileges for the organization, an existing active or requires_review approval, and a comment of at least 10 characters.
A source suggestion is refused if the source is marked exhausted or an identical suggestion already exists.
A source suggestion requires a comment of at least 10 characters and referenced entities must exist (S4: molecular profile and therapies must not be deprecated; therapy interaction type rules).
Editors must hold a valid COI statement to change a source suggestion's status (non-editor signed-in users are not blocked).
Source suggestion status may only move new->curated/rejected or curated/rejected->new.
Submitting an evidence item from a source suggestion automatically marks the suggestion curated (and may mark the source fully curated).

controls.rule: Accepting the first evidence item for a submitted source sets the source status to partially curated; suggesting a fully curated source sets it back to partially curated.

absences.note: No rule decides which pending evidence item is reviewed next at any snapshot. Lists of submitted items are only sorted for display (evidence_items index ordered by id asc in S1/S2; curation_dashboard_controller#evidence_items_requiring_action status=submitted ordered by id in S2; GraphQL resolvers with user-chosen sort and an exclude-own-revisions filter in S4). Any editor may moderate any item.

No assignee, reviewer, due-date or deadline field or logic for evidence items at any snapshot (searched models, jobs, controllers, schema for assign/due/deadline/reviewer). Domain expert tags (S1/S2) are only a listing of users, not assignment; role mentions (S4) only notify.

No timer, expiry or scheduled task writes evidence-item status at any snapshot (S1 has no scheduler; S2-S4 config/scheduled_tasks.yml has no such job; S4 retraction job only raises flags). The controls counted here are human exit paths: soft delete guarded by role (E18, S1-S2) and submitter self-withdrawal by rejecting own item (E10, S2-S4). If only automated/timer exits count, all four values are false.

notes: 1) S2 policies receive a UserContext (DelegateClass(User)) as pundit_user, while submitter/flagging_user/suggested_change.user are plain User records; ActiveRecord#== uses instance_of?, so comparisons such as evidence_item.submitter != user (self-acceptance ban E8/A6/R7) and submitter == user (self-reject E10/A7, R9, flag-owner F3) may not behave as written. I coded them as present because the code checks them, but their effect in S2 is uncertain. 2) S2 helper editor_without_coi? actually means editor WITH a valid COI. 3) In S3/S4 the server does not check COI for evidence/assertion moderation (only for revisions, flags, source suggestions, approvals); the client hides buttons (coded as C). 4) S1 role hierarchy is curator<moderator<editor<admin and policies require moderator; S2-S4 is curator<editor<admin. 5) S2 FlagEntity uses first_or_create so a user has at most one open flag per entity (dedup, not refused; not coded). 6) S2 SourcePolicy#update? lets any signed-in user set a source's status (e.g. exhausted), which then blocks suggestions (S1x). 7) S4 DeprecationValidator blocks deprecating diseases/therapies/sources linked to submitted/accepted evidence or open revisions; not coded as a review control. 8) E13 in S3 covers only type-consistency validation; S4 adds retraction/deprecation. 9) Admin back office (E17) bypasses the self-acceptance and COI rules. 10) Some S4 variant-revision mutations make the comment optional (R2 coded as present based on evidence-item/assertion revisions).
